clue.text: Worker embracing girl in Central American state

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the worker's letters wrap round the girl's

parts.note: a bee is the classic crossword worker (worker bee)
Liz is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A labourer cuddles a young woman somewhere in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a country on the Caribbean coast of Central America, south of Mexico.

clue.text: Mistake made by little brat losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A slip committed by a naughty child who has lost his cool.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Perspicacity one shows at first in period of darkness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the period of darkness

parts.note: night is the period of darkness

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word shows

explanation.surface: A sharp mind is first revealed during a dark spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The S goes inside NIGHT after its N, giving NSIGHT, with I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is deep understanding, the same quality as perspicacity or keen perception.

clue.text: Long to get up for Muslim festival

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means rising, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, hence die

explanation.surface: Yearning to rise early for a religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is the name of the two main Islamic festivals, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.

clue.text: Drink with everyone before work

parts.note: all means everyone
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a drink with the whole group before getting down to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLOP is British slang for beer or strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is informal British slang for beer or other alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Skilled writer's angry talk with German husband

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to have words is to argue angrily
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A writer quarrels with a German husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsmith is a person skilled at using language, especially a professional writer.

clue.text: Old language the French can put together

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue that French speakers can assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome, no longer spoken.

clue.text: Little-known old remedy protecting Bachelor of Surgery

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the old remedy's letters go round the degree

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
BS is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Surgery

explanation.surface: An obscure old treatment that keeps a surgeon out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is not well known, a direct equivalent.

clue.text: Campaigner's appeal accepted by simple king

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the simple word holds the appeal inside

parts.note: crude means simple, unrefined
SA is short for sex appeal
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A political campaigner's charm wins over a plain-speaking monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Mammoth's tooth traveller originally found by Welsh river

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning of the word traveller, its opening letter

parts.note: the Usk is a river in south Wales

explanation.surface: A walker comes across an old mammoth tusk on the banks of a river in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is the long protruding tooth of an elephant or mammoth.

clue.text: Amphibian in river enveloped in thick mist

indicators.note: being enveloped means being wrapped all round, so the river's letter sits inside the mist

parts.note: fog is thick mist

explanation.surface: A creature in a river hidden by heavy fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is a tailless amphibian that lives near water.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid served by graduate liable to err

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
sinful means inclined to go wrong morally

explanation.surface: Drinks poured out by a fallible graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinful is as much liquid as a basin will hold, a measured amount.

clue.text: Inferior porcelain in place of horse trials

parts.note: bad means inferior
Minton is a famous English make of porcelain

explanation.surface: Cheap china on show at an equestrian event.
explanation.walkthrough: MINTON is a Staffordshire pottery and porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton, an estate in Gloucestershire, hosts the famous annual horse trials.

clue.text: Sent on prescribed course and heavily defeated

definitions.meaning: ... as in sent along a set route
... as in put to flight, crushed

explanation.surface: An army marched along a set route and thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has two senses: directed along a route, and beaten soundly in battle.

clue.text: Distinguished actor, one appearing in musical

indicators.note: appearing in puts the one inside the musical's title

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor takes a part in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most acclaimed British stage and screen actors.

clue.text: Trendy act? Absolutely

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stylish action counts, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word of agreement, like certainly.

clue.text: Gather information from society girl on raging fire

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering society

indicators.note: a raging fire is wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Questioning a young socialite about a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them after a mission to get information.

clue.text: Reduce short skirt seen in vessel

indicators.note: the skirt appears inside the vessel, so its letters go within

parts.note: a dish is a vessel for food
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A miniskirt shown shrinking inside a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to make smaller or lessen, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Small detached territory where one's allowed to meet

parts.note: one is I, and 's is a contraction of is: I + S
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A tiny island where people are permitted to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: One's gives I'S, with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, a little piece of land cut off by water.

clue.text: Boyfriend's part of East End, according to report

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the place name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Bow is a district of London's East End

explanation.surface: Someone's boyfriend reportedly comes from the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow, a district in London's East End, is said like BEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male admirer or suitor.

clue.text: Change table, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: speaking points to the spoken word, so the word for the table is taken by its sound

parts.note: an altar is a communion table in a church

explanation.surface: Redescribing a table using a different turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to modify or make different.

clue.text: For example, Sikes's account?

definitions.meaning: ... Sikes is the villain in Dickens's Oliver Twist, so his first name is an example

explanation.surface: A question about what the Dickens villain owes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is an invoice, and Bill is the given name of Dickens's housebreaker Sikes.

clue.text: Holiday-makers — sort Uist cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated land is worked over and turned, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Visitors on holiday tidy up the farmland of Uist, a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists are people travelling for pleasure, especially on holiday.

clue.text: The purpose of American English?

explanation.surface: A wry question about what American English is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Use is the point or function of something, its purpose.

clue.text: Brother at college, one from Saint-Malo, perhaps

parts.note: Eton is the famous English school, Eton College

explanation.surface: A monk at an English school who turns out to be French.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is in Brittany, so a person from there is a Breton; perhaps marks it as one example.

clue.text: Achievement of force invading eastern stronghold

indicators.note: an invader enters territory, so the force's letter goes inside

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A military force storms a fortress in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort can be a thing achieved by exertion, a piece of work done.
